source.title_or_context: Recommendations for pacing in sinus node dysfunction

table_assessment.assessment_notes: Isolated structured table with nine pacing, programming, and ablation recommendations for sinus node dysfunction.

entities.surface_form: patients with SND and a DDD pacemaker

normative_assertions.notes: DECREASE captures minimization of unnecessary ventricular pacing, implemented through pacemaker programming.

text_units.verbatim_text: In patients with SND and a DDD pacemaker, minimization of unnecessary ventricular pacing through programming is recommended.144,151,159,164,166–169

normative_assertions.notes: The recommendation is conditional on clear attribution of symptoms to bradyarrhythmias.

text_units.verbatim_text: Pacing is indicated in SND when symptoms can clearly be attributed to bradyarrhythmias.14,128–131

entities.surface_form: symptomatic patients with the bradycardia–tachycardia form of SND

normative_assertions.notes: The source states an explicit exception when ablation of the tachyarrhythmia is preferred.

text_units.verbatim_text: Pacing is indicated in symptomatic patients with the bradycardia–tachycardia form of SND in order to correct bradyarrhythmias and enable pharmacological treatment, unless ablation of the tachyarrhythmia is preferred.17,20,21,136–138,170,171

entities.surface_form: patients who present chronotropic incompetence and have clear symptoms during exercise

normative_assertions.notes: The source recommends consideration of DDD rate-responsive pacing under both stated conditions.

text_units.verbatim_text: In patients who present chronotropic incompetence and have clear symptoms during exercise, DDD with rate-responsive pacing should be considered.172,173

entities.surface_form: patients with AF-related bradycardia or symptomatic pre-automaticity pauses

normative_assertions.notes: The OCR-visible phrase 'pre-automaticity pauses' is retained exactly and requires human adjudication; avoiding pacemaker implantation is the stated intended outcome.

text_units.verbatim_text: AF ablation should be considered as a strategy to avoid pacemaker implantation in patients with AF-related bradycardia or symptomatic pre-automaticity pauses, after AF conversion, taking into account the clinical situation.136–139,174

entities.surface_form: patients with the bradycardia–tachycardia variant of SND

normative_assertions.notes: The modal 'may' supports permissive force for consideration of atrial ATP programming.

text_units.verbatim_text: In patients with the bradycardia–tachycardia variant of SND, programming of atrial ATP may be considered.164,165

normative_assertions.notes: The pause-duration threshold and documented sinus arrest are explicit applicability conditions; reduced recurrent syncope is the intended outcome.

text_units.verbatim_text: In patients with syncope, cardiac pacing may be considered to reduce recurrent syncope when asymptomatic pause(s) >6 s due to sinus arrest is documented.133,134

normative_assertions.notes: The source explicitly qualifies both symptom attribution and evidentiary conclusiveness.

text_units.verbatim_text: Pacing may be considered in SND when symptoms are likely to be due to bradyarrhythmias, when the evidence is not conclusive.

entities.surface_form: patients with bradyarrhythmias related to SND that are asymptomatic or due to transient causes that can be corrected and prevented
transient causes that can be corrected and prevented

normative_assertions.notes: AGAINST applies to performing pacing in either asymptomatic or correctable/preventable transient-cause presentations described by the source.

text_units.verbatim_text: Pacing is not recommended in patients with bradyarrhythmias related to SND that are asymptomatic or due to transient causes that can be corrected and prevented.33
